description:
Create a verification session

Creates an end-user verification session. Requires an OrgToken and a callback subscription; pass providers, context, and an optional registered verificationClientUrl (omitted: the Portal). Send the end user to the returned verificationUrl; that is where they verify. Billing refusal returns 402 or 429 with event billing_required and a terminal sessionId.

body.description: Body for `POST /verifications/sessions`. Authenticated by the consumer's `OrgToken`. Carries no callback URLs — they come from the org's callback subscriptions. The one shared `context` is validated against every provider's `requiredContext`.

context.description: Consumer context, shared by all providers. Validated against EACH resolved provider version's `requiredContext` JSON Schema (a 400 is returned on mismatch); extra fields are always allowed. Recipe requests resolve scalar values as `{{context.key}}`, then `{{context_key}}`, then `{{key}}`. A lower-priority alias is used only when the recipe doesn't use a higher-priority spelling; an explicit parameter takes precedence. Echoed back (plus `reclaimSessionId`) in the result. Builder-owned `reclaimSessionId` and `attestationNonce` remain context-only.

diagnostics.description: Optional; omit or send false for a normal session. Opts this session into diagnostic mode. A diagnostic session records more event detail, including personal data such as the claimant's IP addresses (see ClaimantDetails.network). Builder appends `diag=1` to the returned `verificationUrl` for a diagnostic session and strips any `diag` value the Consumer's own `verificationClientUrl` carries, so this field — not the URL — is the only way to turn diagnostics on. Treat a diagnostic verification URL as sensitive, and don't hand it to a claimant by default.

launchOptions.description: Where a Verification Client sends the claimant's browser at the end of a flow. Builder stores these on the session and returns them unchanged (see VerificationSession.launchOptions / BootstrapVerificationClient) — it never reads them itself, never redirects a claimant to them, and never executes them; only the Verification Client that renders the flow does. Vocabulary matches `reclaim-js-sdk`'s `VerificationRequest` and `reclaim-portal`'s `parseVerificationLaunch`: `redirectUrl`/`redirectUrlOptions` on success, `cancelRedirectUrl`/`cancelRedirectUrlOptions` on cancellation. `https:` only — `javascript:`, `data:`, and any other scheme are rejected with 400 at session creation.

cancelRedirectUrl.description: Where to send the claimant after a cancelled verification.

cancelRedirectUrlOptions.description: How a Verification Client performs a launch-options redirect — a plain GET (default) or a form POST/GET carrying extra fields. Matches `reclaim-portal`'s `HttpRedirectionOptions`.

redirectUrl.description: Where to send the claimant after a successful verification.

redirectUrlOptions.description: How a Verification Client performs a launch-options redirect — a plain GET (default) or a form POST/GET carrying extra fields. Matches `reclaim-portal`'s `HttpRedirectionOptions`.

preferAiAgent.description: When true, the Builder verification page runs the AI authoring agent instead of the providers' structured recipes. A proven recipe is published only for the provider's own organization; for any other provider it is submitted for admin review. Omit it to run the stored recipes.

preferredLocale.description: Optional locale override for this verification session. It takes precedence over the organization theme's preferred locale.

providers.description: Providers to verify, in run order. The Verification Client runs each sequentially in one browser session and submits one combined result; all are required. Provider version constraints are resolved only while this request is created; clients receive the exact immutable resolved versions and never resolve them again.

items.description: A provider (+ optional version) to verify in a session.

version.description: Empty selects the latest active trunk version. An exact semantic version pins that version. Any other valid npm semantic-version range selects the highest active matching version.

verificationClientUrl.description: Optional. Must exactly equal the base URL of a registered verification client (see the `verification_clients` registry / `/admin/verification-clients`). Omit to use the default (`portals`) client. The Builder resolves and stores the registered client UUID, then returns the ready-to-share `verificationUrl` with the session id and `api=2`. A URL that is not a registered client's base is rejected with 400. Consumers append any client-owned redirect parameters after receiving the URL; Builder does not manage them. The built-in clients are `{origin}/share/{name}`, listed in the examples.

orgToken.description: The organization API key (`rorg_…`) this call authenticates with: from `issue_org_token`, or the app's RECLAIM_ORG_SECRET. Defaults to the MCP server's RECLAIM_ORG_SECRET. Never echo it back to the user.

name: create_verification_session
